rights.notes: Only independently written factual metadata and outbound links are redistributed; no source prose or creative asset is copied.

review.notes: Claims were checked against the linked primary or regulatory source. Evidence and causality are stated conservatively; independent human review is encouraged.

objective: Challenge the assumption that laundry and household work belong primarily to women.
audience: men and women sharing domestic responsibilities
businessContext: Household labor in India was commonly framed as women's work, creating a social norm directly adjacent to the detergent category.
strategy: Use the brand's category role to make unequal household labor visible and invite men to participate.
outcomes: P&G reports that the campaign continued for more than seven years and that the measured social norm shifted over that period.
whatWorked: The social issue was tightly connected to product use.
A repeatable platform allowed the message to evolve rather than end after one burst.
whatFailed: The cited company report does not isolate campaign incrementality from broader social change.
transferConditions: The brand has a credible role in the behavior it asks people to change.
nonTransferConditions: Do not copy the purpose framing into a category with no credible link to the issue.

sources.title: P&G 2023 Citizenship Report
sources.methodology: Company report documents the campaign's launch, duration and reported norm shift; it is not an independent incrementality study.

economicContext: India; broader economic effects are not isolated

outcomeMeasurements.name: Reported shift in the household-labor norm after seven campaign years
